the effects of cumulative adversity on older adults' mental and physical well being are stronger in collectivist cultures, and that the effect of other oriented adversity is stronger than the effect of self-oriented adversity.

the effects of cumulative adversity on mental and psychological health, and its implications to the health of older people in different cultures.
the effects of cumulative adversity across the life span on the health of older adults, and the moderating effects of cultural background on these effects.
the effects of the accumulation of adversities that target either the self or others on the mental and health of older adults, and the role of cultural background in this process.

the effects of cumulative adversity on mental and health health may differ among individuals from collectivist and individualist societies.

the accumulation of adversity that primarily affects the self has a stronger impact on health than adversity that primarily targets others, but this is true for both collectivist and individualist societies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of other oriented adversity on health may depend on the cultural background, but not the effect of self- oriented adversity.
the accumulation of adversities, which are self oriented in nature, has similar effects on the health of older adults from individualist and collectivist cultures.
the effect of cumulative other oriented adversity on the mental health of older adults is more severe in collectivist cultures, such as the Arab culture in Israel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cultural background moderates not only the effect of self-oriented adversity but also the effect of other-oriented adversity.
cultural background moderates how the effect of adversity on health unfolds across the life span.
cultural factors should be taken into account when studying how adversity affects health, particularly in cross cultural studies.
